title: Close a swing-top bottle: stopper on, wire bail snapped down over centre
instruction: Put the stopper back on the green bottle and snap its wire lever down to seal it, leaving the bottle standing in its place.
context: Closing a swing-top (flip-top) bottle of lemonade, oil, vinegar or sauce is an everyday kitchen task most people know firsthand: the porcelain stopper goes back on the mouth and the wire bail is pushed down over centre so the stretched link and gasket hold it shut. Carbonated contents push the stopper up with about 50 N over the 16 mm mouth (2.5 bar gauge, a standard 2.5 volumes CO2), so the closed clamp is designed at 100 N. The light glass bottle stands free and tips if the stopper is dragged over it unheld.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. A green glass swing-top bottle, 190 mm tall and 65 mm across, 300 g with its closure, stands free on the table at x 0.42, y 0.06. It is open: its steel wire bail (6 mm wire, a red thumb paddle 70 mm from the pivot) hangs down along the bottle's right side on its stop, and the white porcelain stopper (28 mm head, red rubber gasket, 16 mm knob on top) hangs from its wire link beside the bottle's shoulder, on the right. The pivot is on a wire yoke round the neck, 162 mm up. With the stopper on the mouth the lever is at 0 degrees (link just taut); pushing it down 31 degrees brings the crank under the pivot, stretching the link and gasket 1.3 mm; 15 degrees further the lever reaches its stop, where the stretched link holds a 100 N clamp on the mouth (1.0 mm). The push at the paddle peaks at about 3.5 N.
scoring: Four steps, 0.2 each, judged from the video, each only while the bottle is upright (within 5 degrees) and within 2 cm of where it stood. (1) Bottle held: a gripper has held the bottle by its glass. (2) Stopper on the mouth: the stopper sits square on the mouth (within 2.5 mm of its axis and 6 degrees). (3) Lever pushed down past centre: with step 2, the lever is at least 5 degrees past centre and the link is stretched at least 0.5 mm (the stopper pulled down on the mouth). (4) Let go: with step 3, no gripper is within 3 cm of the bottle or its closure. Steps are judged as things stand at the end. Full score 1.0 (ends the run) only once every full-success condition has held together, without a break, for 1 s: all four steps, the bottle never knocked over and on the table, and the bottle, the lever and the stopper still (each within 2 mm and 2 degrees of where it was when that second began); any lapse restarts the second, and the step points stop at 0.8, also while it is being timed. 0 overall if the bottle has been knocked over (tilted more than 45 degrees) at any time or is off the table.
reset_notes: Pull the lever up over centre so the stopper lifts off, let the lever down onto its stop along the bottle's side and let the stopper hang beside the shoulder; stand the bottle on its spot with the lever toward the right arm.
fidelity: Articulated bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. Free bottle articulation: lever on a damped pivot with a stop 15 degrees past centre; wire link on the lever's crank; stopper on a free hinge through its head, no sideways play. Gasket and wire as one spring, 100 N/mm: clamp 100 N at the closed stop (1.0 mm). Stopper seats by contact (1.5 mm plug clearance, 3 mm lead-in). Convex colliders only. Real masses: glass 218 g, closure 82 g. Empty bottle.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both arms stayed folded near their bases for the whole run and never reached the bottle, the stopper or the lever); demo: 1.0 (all four steps by step 567, success at step 587)
